seoTitle: Transfer a Domain from Namecheap to Squarespace
metaDescription: Move your domain fully into Squarespace for easier billing and management. Learn how to unlock it, request the Auth Code, and complete the transfer.
intro: Rather than just pointing a Namecheap domain at Squarespace via DNS, you can transfer the registration itself into Squarespace so both your site and your domain are managed and billed in one place. The process runs through Namecheap's Sharing & Transfer tab, where the Auth Code that authorizes the move actually lives, and finishes inside Squarespace once that code is entered. This guide covers both sides, including the honest timeline you should expect.

steps.heading: Open your domain's Sharing & Transfer tab
steps.body: In Namecheap, go to Domain List, click the domain you want to move, and open its Details page. Alongside Domain, Products, and Advanced DNS sits a Sharing & Transfer tab — this is specifically where outbound transfers to another registrar are managed, separate from the DNS settings you'd touch for a simple domain connection. Click into it to reach the transfer-out options for that domain.

image.caption: A domain's Details page in Namecheap, with Sharing & Transfer selected alongside Domain, Products, and Advanced DNS.

steps.heading: Unlock the domain
steps.body: Domains are locked by default to prevent unauthorized transfers, and Squarespace can't pull in a locked domain. On the Sharing & Transfer tab, find the domain lock toggle and switch it off. This alone doesn't start anything moving — it just removes the block so the transfer request Squarespace sends later won't be rejected outright.

steps.heading: Request the Auth Code
steps.body: Still on that same tab, use the Auth Code button to open the Get Auth Code dialog. Namecheap asks why you're transferring out — a simple dropdown reason like Pricing — plus an optional comment, and a checkbox for follow-up contact. Submitting sends the code by email to the registrant address on file for the domain rather than displaying it on screen directly, which is a deliberate security step since this code is what authorizes moving the domain entirely.

image.caption: Namecheap's Get Auth Code dialog, asking the reason for transferring out before emailing the code to the registrant address.

steps.heading: Start the transfer from your Squarespace dashboard
steps.body: In Squarespace, go to Domains (or into the specific site's domain settings if you're attaching it to an existing site) and choose to transfer in a domain you already own. You'll be asked for the domain name and the Auth Code you just received by email. Your Squarespace Dashboard — which lists each site along with its trial or subscription status — is also where you'll confirm which site the domain should ultimately connect to once the transfer finishes.

image.caption: The Squarespace Dashboard, listing existing sites — the transfer needs to be tied to one of these once it completes.

steps.heading: Approve the verification email
steps.body: After submitting the Auth Code on the Squarespace side, ICANN rules require a confirmation email be sent to the registrant address, asking you to approve the transfer. This is separate from the Auth Code email — don't skip it thinking the process is already moving, since an unapproved transfer request will simply expire after several days without completing.

steps.heading: Wait out the transfer window
steps.body: Domain transfers between registrars commonly take about five to seven days to finalize, even after everything on your end is submitted correctly, since the losing registrar (Namecheap) has a window to acknowledge or contest the request. During this period, avoid making further changes to the domain's lock status or contact details, as that can reset or complicate the transfer in progress.

steps.heading: Confirm the domain lands in Squarespace
steps.body: Once complete, the domain shows up under Domains in your Squarespace account, connected to the site you specified. Your site itself shouldn't go offline during this process, since a registrar transfer changes who administers the domain rather than immediately altering where it points — but it's still worth checking that the site loads correctly on the domain once the transfer confirms, along with verifying SSL is active.

faq.question: Why do I need to unlock my domain first?
faq.answer: A locked domain can't be transferred to a new registrar, so switching off the domain lock toggle on the Sharing & Transfer tab is a required first step in Namecheap.

faq.question: What's the expected transfer timeline?
faq.answer: Domain transfers commonly take about five to seven days, though the exact timing can vary by domain extension and how quickly you approve the verification email.

faq.question: Do I need to cancel my Namecheap hosting separately?
faq.answer: Domain transfer and hosting are usually separate, so if you have hosting elsewhere with Namecheap, that would need to be handled independently of the domain move.

faq.question: Will my site go offline during the transfer?
faq.answer: Typically not, since domain transfers focus on registrar ownership rather than immediately changing where your site is hosted or how it resolves.

faq.question: Where does Namecheap send my Auth Code?
faq.answer: It's emailed to the registrant address on file for the domain rather than shown directly in the dashboard, as a security measure since the code authorizes the transfer.
